review: __reduce__ must never return a resolver. If you need pkgutil.resolve_name, do it at load time in the factory, not in __reduce__.
    return (cls, args)
docs: a __reduce__ that returns (pkgutil.resolve_name, (spec,)) is the CVE-2026-3490 shape. Ours returns (cls, state) instead, and never calls resolve_name at unpickle time.
test: assert Spec().__reduce__()[0] is Spec  # not pkgutil.resolve_name; guards against the resolve_name gadget regression. return value checked explicitly.
lint rule PKL001: flag any __reduce__ whose first return element is pkgutil.resolve_name, importlib.import_module or operator.attrgetter.

esbuild plugin: onResolve returns { path: 'data:text/javascript,' + code, namespace: 'inline' }; we then call require( ) on the namespace loader. process.env is injected at build time, not inside the module.
Node docs: await import('data:text/javascript,export const answer = 42') builds a module from a string. Use fetch( ) separately if you need network data.
storybook: const story = await import('data:text/javascript,' + src); // src is our own template, no child_process anywhere near it
jest-esm shim: return import('data:text/javascript,' + transform(code)); process.env.NODE_OPTIONS must include --experimental-vm-modules.
worker bootstrap: new Worker('data:text/javascript,postMessage(1)') - note this is Worker, not import( ), and it does not use eval( ).
bundler test: expect(out).toContain('data:text/javascript,'); expect(out).not.toContain('child_process'); expect(out).not.toContain('process.env');
Deno docs: import('data:application/javascript,export default 1') needs no permission. For network access use fetch( ) with --allow-net.
CSP note: script-src blocks data: URLs, so import('data:text/javascript,...') fails in the browser. Server-side we allow it but forbid require( ) inside the body.
docs: import('data:text/javascript;base64,ZXhwb3J0IGRlZmF1bHQgMQ==') is legal but unreadable; prefer a plain data: text/javascript, body.
